question: Claude keeps quoting a superseded pricing sheet that someone uploaded to a shared Project several months ago. Which two actions address the cause? Select two.
options: A) Remove the superseded pricing sheet from the Project's knowledge so it stops being used.
B) Switch the Project over to a deeper-reasoning tier so the wrong figures get caught in future.
C) Upload the current pricing sheet so that the Project draws on the version now in force.
D) Add a line to every chat telling Claude to ignore any pricing figure that looks wrong.
E) Start a brand new Project every month so that old uploads never have time to accumulate.
correct_answers: A) Remove the superseded pricing sheet from the Project's knowledge so it stops being used.
C) Upload the current pricing sheet so that the Project draws on the version now in force.
explanations: Correct. The stale document is the cause, so removing it from the knowledge base is what actually stops the wrong figures.
Incorrect. A deeper tier reasons better over whatever it is given, and it is still being given the superseded sheet.
Correct. Replacing it with the current sheet gives the Project the right source, which is the other half of the same fix.
Incorrect. Re-prompting cannot fix a wrong source document; Claude has no way to know which figure is out of date.
Incorrect. Discarding the workspace monthly throws away the accumulated context and still does not curate the sources.
